record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Does every F-space contain a subspace M such that the quotient space X/M has nontrivial continuous linear functionals?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 15. - Does each F-space contain a subspace such that there are nontrivial linear continuous functionals in the quotient space ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An F-space is a topological vector space $X$ over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$) whose topology is induced by a complete, translation-invariant metric. A continuous linear functional on $X$ is a continuous linear map $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ (resp. $\mathbb{C}$); the zero functional is called trivial. For a closed linear subspace $M\subseteq X$, the quotient $X/M$, equipped with the quotient topology, is again an F-space.

Question: Does every F-space $X$ contain a closed linear subspace $M\subsetneq X$ such that the quotient F-space $X/M$ admits a nontrivial continuous linear functional?
artifact.category_tag: F-spaces and non-locally convex topological vector spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references in the theory of F-spaces (notably the monograph "An F-space Sampler" by Kalton, Peck, and Roberts, and Kalton–Roberts' construction of rigid subspaces of $L_0$) develop techniques relevant to this question, and Kalton constructed F-spaces with trivial dual. However, no source consulted explicitly states a definitive answer to whether every F-space has a quotient with nontrivial continuous linear functionals, so the present status could not be confirmed.

status_evidence.title: An F-space Sampler
status_evidence.snippet: Theory motivated by spaces L_p for 0 ≤ p < 1; questions about the size of the dual space are especially important in the non-locally convex setting.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of duals of F-spaces and their quotients is a central theme; no explicit resolution of this specific question is stated.

status_evidence.title: Nigel Kalton Memorial – Publications
status_evidence.snippet: Kalton, 'An F-space with trivial dual where the Krein–Milman theorem holds'; Kalton–Roberts, 'A rigid subspace of L_0'.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on F-spaces with trivial dual and rigid subspaces of $L_0$ exist but do not directly settle the quotient question.
